subject: AcreetionOS Update — July 08, 2026
body:
Emacs 31.1 has just been released, bringing a plethora of changes and improvements to the iconic editor, and our community is already exploring its potential. This release is a significant milestone, and you can learn more about the changes and updates on our wiki page at https://acreetionos.org/wiki.html, which is constantly being updated with the latest information and guides.

Development 
The recent enhancements to our continuous integration pipeline have been focused on improving the reliability and stability of our ISO build process, with the introduction of per-pipeline staging directories and relative symlinks for the latest.iso file. These changes have significantly reduced the likelihood of publish races between concurrent builds, and you can find more details about these updates on our changelog page at https://acreetionos.org/changelog.html.

Community 
Our community has been actively engaged in discussions and contributions, with recent security updates and kernel releases being closely followed and integrated into our distribution. You can stay up-to-date with the latest news and updates on our website at https://acreetionos.org/, and explore our documentation at https://acreetionos.org/docs.html for more information on how to get involved and contribute to the project. Tip of the day: if you're looking to try out the latest Emacs release, you can find it in our repositories, and our flash page at https://acreetionos.org/flash.html has some useful tips and tricks for getting the most out of your AcreetionOS experience.
